text:
did you get this one yet? intent amplifier: two decisions expand to N correct elements via topology the editor already knows. That's exactly the right design axis for agents, because agents are bad at exactly the things it eliminates — long ephemeral id lists, per-element loops, and re-reading elements between steps. Here's the family it belongs to:

Selection amplifiers (few picks → many elements)
Your two-vert span, generalized:

Bash
tools/seat action select-path '{"from":12,"to":47}'          # shortest edge-walk between verts
tools/seat action select-path '{"from":12,"to":47,"axis":"y"}' # constrained to monotone axis travel
Reply the computed vert/edge chain as a preview before it becomes the selection — same plan/apply feel as uv-prestack, so the agent verifies the walk matched intent.

Loop and ring from one seed (the classic modeling amplifiers, and you have cut walking rings already — expose the walk as pure selection):

Bash
tools/seat action select-loop '{"edge":31}'      # follow the loop until it closes or hits a pole/boundary
tools/seat action select-ring '{"edge":31}'      # parallel edges across quads
tools/seat action select-boundary '{"face":12}'  # the open perimeter of this component
Replies should state why the walk stopped (terminated:"pole vertex 88" / "boundary" / "closed") — that's diagnostic data an agent uses to plan the next step.

Between two loops:

Bash
tools/seat action select-between '{"loopA":[...],"loopB":[...]}'  # the face band bounded by two loops
This is the retopo corridor primitive — "everything from the shoulder line to the waist line" as one call.

Grow/shrink/similar:

Bash
tools/seat action select-grow '{"rings":2}'                    # expand by adjacency
tools/seat action select-similar '{"by":"normal","tolerance":10}'  # or "area","region","coplanar"
select-similar by:coplanar from one seed face replaces the brittle inside:box dance for isolating a flat panel.

Mirror-twin pick: one vert selected, its reflection auto-joins the selection (you have the twin machinery from bilateral mirror already — expose it as a selection op, for use when mirror-edit isn't armed).

Edit amplifiers (one gesture → correct distributed effect)
Proportional/falloff move — the biggest one missing:

Bash
tools/seat action move-soft '{"delta":[0,0.05,0],"radius":0.3,"falloff":"smooth"}'
Moving one vert with falloff is how organic adjustment actually happens; without it the agent must compute per-vert deltas itself (→ bun escape). Constrain falloff to edge-connected distance, not euclidean, so it never bleeds across a gap onto a neighboring shell.

Constrained slide — move that can't break the surface:

Bash
tools/seat action slide '{"along":"edge","amount":0.5}'    # vert slides along its edge, 0..1
tools/seat action slide '{"along":"surface","delta":[...]}'  # reprojected onto the local surface
Agents constantly want "nudge this vert along the rail without changing the silhouette" and currently can only approximate it with raw move + eyeballed axis.

Flatten / straighten / space — the alignment family (normalize-widths is already one member):

Bash
tools/seat action flatten '{"plane":"best-fit"}'        # or explicit plane — verts project onto it
tools/seat action straighten '{}'                       # selected chain onto the line through its endpoints
tools/seat action space-evenly '{"axis":"y"}'           # equalize gaps along an axis
tools/seat action set-position '{"axis":"y","value":0.75}'  # absolute coordinate for all selected
set-position deserves emphasis: agents think in target coordinates ("tabletop at 0.75 m") but the tool only offers relative move, forcing read-bbox → subtract → move. Absolute placement deletes that whole loop, and its scale/rotate cousins (set-size, set-angle) delete the same loop for dimensions.

Repeat-per-element:

Bash
tools/seat action for-each '{"selector":"region:rivet","do":{"action":"scale-uniform","args":{"factor":0.8}}}'
One decision applied per instance/component, instead of a 40-row batch the agent must generate (and get one id wrong in).

Why this family specifically pays off for agents
Notice the common structure: the agent supplies intent (2 picks, a target value, a seed), the editor supplies topology (the walk, the falloff, the loop). Every op in this family:

Shrinks the error surface — 2 ids the agent just read beat 40 ids it must keep consistent across a generation bump;
Eliminates elements round-trips — the walk happens host-side, so it works on meshes too dense to page across the socket;
Is self-verifying — the reply can state what was computed (spanned 14 verts, terminated at boundary) and the agent checks that sentence instead of re-deriving geometry.
Two implementation notes that matter more than which ops you pick:

Preview-by-default. Every amplifier should return its computed set (count, endpoints, termination reason, bbox) so a wrong walk is caught before the edit, not after. For the mutation forms, your existing token plan/apply pattern fits perfectly.
Deterministic tie-breaking, stated in the reply. "Shortest path" and "loop continuation" have ambiguous cases (equal-length walks, 5-valence verts). Whatever rule breaks the tie, the reply should name it — an agent that knows why it got this walk can correct course; one that gets a silent arbitrary choice will undo-loop.
resolution: Built the intent-amplifier family Zig-first: the agent supplies intent (two picks, a seed edge, a target coordinate) and the host supplies the topology walk, which is what removes the long ephemeral id lists, per-element loops and elements round-trips agents are worst at. Five walks live in framework/gpu/mesh_edit.zig on the same welded topology the overlay trusts, so they work on meshes far too dense to page across the socket: select-path with an optional monotone axis constraint, select-loop on the quad-loop rule, select-ring across quads, select-grow by adjacency, and select-similar by normal, coplanar or area. Both implementation rules the design called for are in: every walk previews by default and stages nothing until --apply hands back the matching token, whose folded-in facecount turns a topology change between preview and apply into a refusal rather than a different set; and every reply names why the walk stopped (closed, boundary, pole, unreached, plus the vertex) and the tie-break rule that resolved ambiguity. Two more amplifiers needed no host work: set-position gives absolute placement with a min/center/max anchor and deletes the read-bbox-subtract-move loop, and for-each applies one decision per matching Outliner part because parts survive the generation bump each step causes. A real bug surfaced while building — model_paint.positions() is not a stride-8 soup and reading it as one produced 45-degree normals for an axis-aligned cube, so face geometry now goes through the welded corner-to-vertex path. Deferred with reasons: move-soft, slide and the flatten/straighten/space-evenly family all need a per-vertex position-write door that does not exist yet, and select-between should follow select-loop.
